[/u]  [h3] So, let’s guess which players bear this cost? [/h3]
[b] Any promotions and announcements from the studio based in English are a mask of hypocrisy as they have never released the same content in Chinese, [/b] even though this is a Chinese studio. [u] Some people posted videos on China's YouTube (some of you may have heard of it, namely bilibili) exposing the company's different treatment of English users and Chinese players. An absolutely amazing party game providing hours of fun for anyone, with some toxicity (propelled by the game itself) and basically zero offline support.

[h2]The good[/h2]

I think Party Animals is an immensely fun game, I really enjoy playing it, especially with friends in custom games. Custom games have support for bots (with three difficulty levels), making games with even 2-3 human players fun and chaotic. There's a lot of variety through maps and the newly introduced Smash and Mario Kart-esque Nemo Kart game modes. The game supports local split-screen play, albeit it's a bit limited, see below. While there are micro-transactions, they are cosmetic-only, and the game allows you to earn some of its premium currency, too, through level ups and achievements, which I think is a very nice addition - I have been able to buy skins that cost premium currency only by playing the game.

There is also a "friend pass", which lets anyone download the game for free, and play with you when you invite them, basically giving you two copies of the game for the price of one. They can do the tutorial on their own and then join a game you invite them to, and even progress.

[h2]The not-so-good[/h2]

As for the negatives, which will be much longer, but not because I think the game is bad. I'm hoping that my review will not only help those looking at buying this game, but also the developers.

1. [b]The game is still online-only[/b], for which it has been criticized heavily. My biggest gripe with it is that even a supposedly local game in custom match mode, where I'm the only player, is still running through the internet: if my connection is shaky, my character will lag. We played with friends in split-screen through Wi-Fi in a custom game with bots, and it was unplayable. This can be a serious gripe for those looking for offline fun: you cannot play this game without a stable internet connection, not even custom games, where you cannot complete weekly quests (though you earn XP). I wish the developers leaned a bit more into making at least custom games offline-accessible, even if there was no progression while the game is offline. Also, you create a separate profile (account) in the game, which is a bit weird. Deep Rock Galactic did this much better with all data being in your save files (and thus tied to your Steam account), though that game has less micro-transactions and is also not competitive in any way.

2. [b]Split-screen[/b]. It works, but not in every game mode, and it's a bit basic. For example, the months-old Smash and Nemo Kart game modes (at the time of writing) still cannot be played in split-screen. The game simply tells you that you cannot do that with local players. Second, since most maps are relatively small, it would make sense to do some dynamic split screen or even play on one big screen, but you are limited to always being split. This is a bit disadvantageous, as the screen is split horizontally in the middle (the two screens are next to each other), severely limiting horizontal view, which is essential to get a grasp of the (usually quite chaotic) situation around you (you don't look much up and down, but you do have to look left and right a lot). This is only an issue with 2 players, as with 3 or 4, you have your regular screen aspect ratio for your view. Playing with friends on a large screen works, though.

3. [b]The (luckily not that huge) toxicity[/b]. I am happy that voice chat can be turned off as-is (I did so when first booting up the game), which from today, requires a verified phone number to use anyway. I wish we could disable text chat, too, or at least limit it to team only. While the occasional emote spamming and "ez" text chats aren't too common (luckily I encounter these in about less than 1 of 5 matches), I think the developers could greatly reduce the remaining toxicity by removing quests that require you to win games - especially since these quests are usually the ones that give you "regular" currency, and this is the only way to earn it besides progression. The other quests ("play X games as an animal that can dive" and such) are really creative, and if only these were left in, I'm sure it would ease the tension. It's a bit easy to get hooked and focus on just winning the game, and I think it's partly due to the quests that are tied to victory.

4. [b]The (absence of) changelogs[/b]. The game is frequently updated, but patch logs are often not supplied with the updates. We've had one when the Nemo Kart game mode was introduced, for example, but for smaller changes, we usually don't get any. I've just found out that the previously Last Stand (4 teams of 2 players) "Ice breaker" map was changed to play out with 2 teams of 4 players, but I've never seen a patch log mentioning this.

[h2]Verdict[/h2]

Buy this game if you're into party games and have at least one friend. Solo, and become toxic in quick matches. Great game, lots of cute animals (skins), fun, sometimes quirky physics-based mechanics and smooth gameplay.

I've waited. A good long while for this game to come out. Played the beta in 2020. Immediately fell in love with the style and a new game to the party brawlers. Waited patiently for 3 more years. Missed the first playtest. Played the next 2, and let me tell you. This game is a mixed bag. I like the game at its core, but everything else is muddied and I dont know how to feel about it. Let me explain. 
[h3] What I liked [/h3] 
[list]

[*] The gameplay. Its fun! It's a TON of fun. Its Gang Beasts meets Fall Guys. Its fun and easy to get into. Theres a lot of powerful items and moves, but the randomness in the physics and the large amount of players. Means theres still a pretty low skill ceiling and approachable to everyone.

[*] The style! Its so cute. Its a very pretty game and the fluffy animals beating the absolute piss out of each others is a fun spectacle.

[*] The maps! While I havent played much of the new maps. The maps that were in the beta. Were fun, unique, had a neat gimmick to them. Theyre well designed and fun to fight in.
[/list]
Unfortunately that's where my positives end and my gripes begin. 
[h3] What I don't Like. [/h3]
[list]
[*] No offline. Yep a game claiming that it has singleplayer and had offline local coop. It in fact. Doesnt. I would say I'm hurt by a company lying. If it werent so ****ing common nowadays. So no local coop unless you got a connection. What a joke. Gang Beasts had that sorted and that game is almost 10 years old now.

[*] Microtransactions. Now I get it. A company has to cover its costs somehow. It still feels grimy that a paid indie game has paid cosmetics and a full fledged shop. When problems exist in the game and they lie about offline coop. I know offline isnt in the game because they worry about you cheating past their store. Thankfully. Its not an entirely bad shop. Currency is earned in game for free by leveling up, and the free currency you earn can be used to unlock decent skins as well. As well as unlocking skins completing challenges. Still tho. With a game like this. Saying "skins for animals" just is weird to me. IMO tho. 

[*] Lootboxes.......****ing really? Pay 120 of your party animal fun bucks or whatever and get a randomized skin. Why? You already have a fortnite item shop. Did you really have to finish it off with that? We left that shit with Battlefront 2. 

[*] The gamemodes. Look. I want to beat the piss out of my fellow animal. Thats it. The other gamemodes are a complete waste on me because, like fall guys. I dont want to team up with strangers that wont do the objective. They want to beat the piss out of their fellow man too. Not play bootleg FIFA or Lucio Ball. They tend to either last 10 seconds as the team stomps the other. Or drags on all the way to the end timer and just isnt fun at all. 

[*] The quit penalty. This game isn't Valorant or CSGO. Why is there a leave penalty when people can join mid match if someone leaves? If someone (like me) doesnt want to play buzzball or soccer for the 2rd or 3th time in a row and want to play the elimination style modes instead.
[/list]
[h3] My suggestions [/h3]
[list] 
[*] Make the Team game modes separate. Fall guys did it so you can queue into those modes. So friends wanting to work with each other. Can. The gamemodes are fun, just not when playing all the time. Separate the game modes and adjust the XP gains to incentives team modes. Or if you dont want to do any of that. Just make it a best of 5. First team to 3 wins. Its that easy. Shortens the length. If you are getting stomped it ends sooner, and close match games can happen much more frequent. I would actually stick around to play them out. 

[*] Remove the quit penalty. Theres no reason for it. There is no rank system at all. We aint competing for the world cup. It'll be of no issue to get rid of it. 

[*] Work on offline ASAP. You told us it would be here on launch. It isn't. That doesn't sit well with anyone. 

[*] Make sure you maintain the currency gained so that people who do put in the time with this game dont feel cheated and the need to buy skins (tho thats exactly what you want isnt it?) I dont think the microtransactions are inherently scummy, but I still hate them in any game.
[/list]
[h3] Closing thoughts [/h3] 
Funnily enough. I enjoy the game. Its fun! Its Fall Guys meets Gang Beasts. The beat em up style gameplay is just fun and chaotic. I will be playing the shit out of this game and I would recommend off the gameplay alone, but with the current issues. I wont at the moment. If you got this far and still decide to get it. All I ask is that you dont support them in their shop. Not until the game is in a better spot and the issues everyone has are addressed.

Thanks for reading!

[h3] Update after one day [/h3]

All my points still stand. Including the leave penalty. The point I forgot to convey was that the game still punishes you. Well before the game starts. So if you see it about to get voted. You just cannot leave w/o punishing. Even tho the game hasnt started and theres still a full minute waiting period that your characters are in a locker room. That should be more than enough time to safely leave a game you dont want to play. That goes for any game mode not just the sports modes. I agree with keeping it after the game has started, but its not needed before.

- Super fun with friends, it's a better, bigger version of gang beasts.

[i]If[/i] you're someone who's on the fence about buying the game or your friends are trying to gaslight you into getting it even though you think you won't enjoy it, I'd say your best bet would be to wait a month or so and keep an eye on the updates & see if the reviews take an upturn. 

[i]If[/i] you have the disposable income, friends[i](optional)[/i] live somewhere there's a server & this won't stop you from buying another game this month, go for it. It's a super fun game best enjoyed with other people not focusing on being competitive I guarantee you'll have a good time.

Party Animals is one of my most played games in my library and I continue to enjoy it on every revisit. But the more I play it, the more I see that it's difficult to recommend to newcomers. On the surface you can imagine that it's a casual party game with cute animals punching each other; however, this is deeply contrasted by the extremely competitive nature of the in-game community. Players who have previous experience with similar physics-based games, such as Gang Beasts or Human Fall Flat, should have a knack for Party Animals and it'd be an easy recommendation. But players with no prior experience should carefully consider if this game is right for them. The following sections of this review will elaborate on my complicated love and hate story with Party Animals.



[u]The Good:[/u]
The fighting controls are more complex than Gang Beasts' and random weapons spawn on the arena to spice up each round. There are several modes to play such as Last Stand (2v2v2v2 or 4v4), Team Score (4v4), and Cabin (for casual off-brand Uno games). The combat is very rewarding once you get a proper handle on it. Exp earned unlocks unique rewards up to level 100, and the achievements also unlock costumes and currency. Players who invest enough time into Party Animals can get around the gacha and game currency limits by gaining experience past level 100 to earn daily mystery boxes containing cookies, Nemo bucks, or lottery coins. I never had a hard time buying the costumes I like in the game's shop because I've earned and saved plenty of currency.

The majority of my hours was spent in solo play but I had more fun whenever I was in a party with friends. Team work is at the heart of each game mode and it's very fun to embrace it with like-minded players. My favorite map of all time is Fluffy Redemption. The respawns are unlimited and there's room for mistakes. I like to switch my roles whenever needed, I could be placing coals into the firebox for a few minutes, attack the opposite team's train to slow them down, and then go back to my train to defend it.

I love the animal and environment physics! Animals can be tossed out of the arena with the right momentum and movement. Each Last Stand map has a hazard that gets deadlier as time passes. Castleween is notable for its random environment destruction. I also enjoy how it's possible to knock out animals with random stuff such as lamps, fishes, and hats. There's no shortage of crazy stuff that can happen in Party Animals. The replayability is practically infinite.



[u]The Bad:[/u]
The initial two hours played on Party Animals may not be enough time to determine if the game is right for some players. In my case, I had a blast during my first 100 hours even while I was solo queuing for matches. But I'm sure newcomers will be frustrated once they encounter the tryhards and toxics in the community.

The matchmaking in Party Animals is split into 2 categories: Quick Match and Custom Games. Custom Games offers limited exp gained daily, and Quick Match allows you to level up indefinitely to level 100 + 3 daily mystery boxes. Custom Games are filled with AI bots and it's not obvious which ones have human players. Quick Match is a very simplified system with no variety of options. You can't select Last Stand or Team Score as the mode you'd prefer to join, and you can't opt to join a queue filled with other solo queue'd players. Instead, Quick Match will join together solo queue'd players with coordinated players in a party, and they'll have to vote on a Last Stand or Team Score map. This creates an environment that throws newcomers into a trial by fire. I've read other players' reviews on Party Animals and I can definitely see where they're coming from: the game turns into a waiting simulator after being eliminated quickly in Last Stand. I find that Team Score modes are more casual than Last Stand, and it'd be a great boon for newcomers if there was a "Quick Match - Team Score" option.

Quick Match is also the only practical way to earn rewards + exp. Winning will award a lot of exp towards a level up, and losing will award very minimal exp regardless of how well you've played. And many of the achievements require amazing feats in Quick Match. Here's an example: "666 - In Buzz Ball, single-handedly accumulate all points for your team and win (Quick Match)." These tryhard achievements contrast the intended spirit of a casual party game. All in all, players are encouraged to play competitively to extremes if they want to earn currency or unique costumes. It's no surprise that there're so many tryhards and toxics, not to the mention the AFK players who farm exp.



[u]My Suggestions to the Devs:[/u][list]
[*] Please add a variety of options to Quick Match. You can divide it into sections: Any Mode, Last Stand, Team Score. This wouldn't mess with the map voting if you filter players into their preferred modes first.
[*] Add a solo queue and party queue option in Quick Match.
[*] Allow players to control both hands independently. (I want to heavy punch with my left hand too!)
[*] Allow players to climb with both hands instead of just jumping while grabbing. (Gang Beasts' climbing is better and more responsive.)[/list]



[u]Conclusion:[/u]
There's a lot to love about Party Animals, but there's also a lot to hate about it. I keep returning to Party Animals because I love physics-based games and platformers. I think the good outweighs the bad, despite having many complaints. Newcomers, on the other hand, should beware of the Quick Matchmaking and the community's git gud attitude. Party Animals' learning curve is pretty high but will reward those who are willing to overcome it. My final rating for the game: 9/10. My rating for the in-game community: 6/10.

Edit: 

The devs responded by pointing out that the game was only playable online during closed testing. I have participated in many closed and open alpha and beta tests and can say this is standard in the industry for a game that hasn't released. Studios typically make playtest builds require internet connection so that they can control when players can access a free copy of the game, stress test servers, collect playtesting data, and avoid the game being accessible early through piracy which is completely reasonable for an unreleased game that noone has bought. With that, an online requirement for an early play test of a game in no way says that the game wouldn't be playable offline on release. As an example COD typically requires you to be online when playing the beta tests however every COD on console has offline play. I would have been shocked if any decent size game was playable offline during playtesting.

But the devs expected me to ignore the product description that specifically said the game was playable offline and judge whether or not the game was playable offline on a closed play test I had access to? - MTX. Unlocking new characters/skins is clearly a money grabbing microtransaction pit, and in order to force us to confront it constantly, we have to live with this terrible always-online business.

In sum:
Party Animals rolled out some nice improvements and made a cuddlier, cleaner game, but the devs immediately crippled it by adding MTX, always-online, and poor local coop support. Maybe try it if theres a super sale for a few bucks, otherwise keep playing Gang Beasts until someone releases a game who actually understands what party gamers want.

[h1] Ok, so lets clear some things up. [/h1]

This game has mixed reviews, which this game [b] definitely does not [/b] deserve. 

Lots of people are giving this game negative reviews because of the fact that the game does not have an 'offline' singe-player mode, or because of the fact that the game has micro-transactions.

[h2] Let's start with the offline single-player mode. [/h2]

To clear things up; the game [b] DOES [/b] support couch split-screen co-op. The only thing it doesn't support is offline play, as you need an online connection to be able to play the game at all. I do understand people being upset about this, as the devs could have been more clear about this, and shouldn't have used the word 'offline' in the game description (which they removed as of now).  

[h2] Micro-transactions [/h2]

In no way is this game pay-to-win. All the micro-transactions in this game are cosmetic, and don't give you an advantage in any way. Matter of fact, both types of currency's are obtainable through just playing the game, and completing weekly/daily challenges! Which means that if you want to spend money to get your characters to look different, go ahead! But it's also obtainable by just playing the game and saving up the currency you get!

[h2] Conclusion [/h2]

Even though i haven't played a lot yet, I can definitely say that I love this game. If you liked Gang Beasts, you're gonna love this one. The gameplay is almost identical, though it feels a little less clunky, and more controllable. Also the fact that this game adds quite some weapons to use, quite a lot of maps on release, and several game-modes to play, makes it so the game doesn't get old quick (which I did have with Gang Beasts). If the devs continue to update the game with more maps, game-modes, weapons and characters (which they are actively doing right now), this game is going to be fun, and fresh for a long time!

If you liked Gang Beasts, you're definitely gonna love this one. Don't let the reviews fool you, the game is a blast! Especially with friends.

[h1]New Players Beware! [/h1]
Please give this a read, I know it's long, but I think it'll help with not only your purchase, but your time.

[h3]Sweats/TryHards Ruin the Game [/h3]

I did enjoy the game a lot in the beginning. The novelty of being little rag doll animals was very fun and entertaining. Soon though the magic wore off as I started to notice how in 85% or more of the matches you would find at least 1 sweatlord (a person who takes the game too seriously and is too competitive) that ruined the fun in any given game mode. It's not about not being able to tolerate a loss, but also the fact of winning a match way too fast. I find myself either being KO'd and thrown out of the round and having to wait until the sweatlord finishes the other people OR the round ends so fast that I didn't get a chance to fully experience the match. The other 15% of the time the games are perfect. There's a back and forth that makes the match fun and satisfying even if it's a loss. It's so rare that it becomes vexing and ultimately you end up giving up. This is BY FAR the biggest reason why I would consider you to not play this game, since it's the main focus on this game.

[h3]FOMO and/or In-game Purchases [/h3]

Thankfully I'm not affected by FOMO, but it's here. I mean, what other game doesn't have this trash at this point. Just wanted you to know it was here. The main problem is the in-game purchases. Yes, you can buy them by just playing the game, but they do give you the option to use real money to get in-game currency. No big deal, right? Well, the bad part is that achieving the in-game currency takes ages to acquire. That's fine for most people that have the time, but for those that don't it becomes a nuisance. What makes it worse is that there are multiple currencies and you only get each type by doing their respective mode! So, not only do you have to play on the main modes, you have to grind in the other modes if you want to get that stuff, too. Yes, you could say, "well, just play the game!", but that's where my point #1 comes peaking its ugly head.

[h3]Toxic Community [/h3]

By far it's not the worst I've experienced and I don't really care for it, but if this kind of stuff affects you, or maybe like your kid or someone you care about then I think it's something to think about. For the most part most are friendly but more often than not you will encounter people that say the worst things and usually masking themselves in a voice changer. And not only the typical inappropriate stuff, but vulgar comments. Spam, messing with people minding their own business, abusing the kick-from-lobby ability, bullying, focusing on a specific person in a match, etc.

In conclusion I just have to emphasize how bad the amount of sweatlords are out there. It truly ruins the game for everyone else. And I get it, they just want to get their achievements for the day or week so they don't care about having fun and that's because of the implemented FOMO and astronomical in-game prices that fuel that toxic behavior. Unless you have the time and willpower to go through with the grind and learning curve then go for it, but honestly I would highly recommend you stay away. Or at least get it super cheap, but still, there are predatory tactics being used in this game, so I wouldn't even get it in a sale if I were you. Thank you for reading, have a great day.

LOCAL MULTIPLAYER IS AN AFTERTHOUGHT

In spite of the impression you might get from watching the trailers, Party Animals was not built with local couch PVP/co-op in mind. Having bought the game to play with my family on the big screen, it was disappointing to see the local/couch multiplayer experience severely lacking in many regards. 

For starters the game is built around online functionality and will not run without an internet connection. The main menu is more or less an online lobby and for any strictly local-play you have to create a new lobby and lock it in order to keep other players out. And even then the best you can hope for is a split-screen experience seeing there is no full-screen multiplayer outside of online play. Which is an odd game design choice for this type of game.

Aside from that, the game is actually really fun to play. It feels sort of like Gang Beasts, but with a significant upgrade. Which makes it even more disappointing they didn't build the game around a solid couch-play experience with family instead of just making local play an afterthought. 

Refund requested, but I will happily purchase Party Animals again if they ever streamline the local multiplayer experience, add offline functionality, and drop the tiny pocket split-screen in favor of full-screen (or something more dynamic). Really poor design choice devs.

TL;DR - Do not buy if you're expecting a party game or want a couch PVP experience like Gangbeasts. This game is exclusively made with online play in mind and it requires an internet connection to play. Two thumbs down.

I really really want to recommend this game, but the state it is in at this very moment I cannot. 

The concept is amazing, and I adore all the cute animals along with the cosmetics that are out, and the collabs they've done. Visually it is a really good, a cute cartoon-y game where you get to be a stuffed animal.

Unfortunately, the community is already incredibly toxic and the game hasn't even been out more than two weeks. I am a girl and I feel like I am in a COD lobby by the amount of hate I get when speaking. It is very common to get cussed out in games and called slurs because you knocked somebody out or are just playing that game the way it is meant to be played, OR because you sound like a girl. [spoiler] [i](If I get told to make one more sandwich I am going to put laxatives in it).[/i] ʘ‿ʘ [/spoiler] 

You would think with the game being about really cute stuffed animals the community would be nice and welcoming, but it's not. You can argue that I should just mute the voice chat or just ignore it, but the game was made with voice chat and I enjoy interacting with the wholesome section of this community, the ones that are just trying to have fun and don't threaten to un-alive you for knocking them out.

And the game play, I could write an entire review just about this. You can pick up a weapon, and it is pretty much game over for everyone else without a weapon unless the weapon holder is miraculously knocked out, or they run out of stamina. If you get nun-chucks or a shovel then it is almost impossible to get close enough to that person to knock them out, especially on maps like the alligator river or airplane, because those are not at all forgiving and one misjudged jump is the end. I think weapons should have some type of cool down or some type of durability at least. There should be no reason a single cat with a pair of nun-chucks can knock out eight people in a row and win the game simply because they were the first person to pick up a weapon. It is ridiculous.

Speaking of being knocked out, what is the point in playing when people can just stand over you and continuously knock you out? There have been many times where somebody is upset and targets me or another person and tries to keep them knocked out for the entirety of that game, and it is incredibly frustrating to stand up only to be drop kicked into the shadow realm once again. 

This is just a quality of life request really, but they should add something in the game where you can see your own stuffed animal better. This would help visually impaired individuals, because sometimes you can lose your own character in the chaos of everyone. Maybe a little glowing outline or something else to better indicate where you are in the group.

Overall, I like the concept of this game. It is cute and fun with friends, but it certainly can be improved. If you are looking to buy it I would wait a little while to see if there are any updates.

🐾 What’s Great

1. The Physics Are Hilarious

The star of the show is the janky, floppy, glorious physics system. You’ll flail, wobble, punch, grab, throw, slide, and sometimes just fall off the map for no reason at all. It’s clumsy on purpose — and that’s what makes it so fun.

Fights often devolve into accidental genius: maybe you swing a shovel and knock your friend off a moving train… or get punched once and spin through the air like a noodle. Every match feels like a new comedy sketch.

2. It’s Genuinely Fun With Friends

Whether you're playing online or locally, Party Animals shines as a party game. It’s one of those rare titles where everyone can join in, regardless of skill. Even the most casual players will end up laughing — or shouting — within minutes.

There’s no steep learning curve. Just jump in, grab a panda, and cause chaos.

3. The Characters Are Ridiculously Cute

From corgis to ducks to dinosaurs in hats, every animal looks like it belongs in a viral plushie line. The cosmetic system lets you unlock new outfits and styles, and yeah… it’s hard not to get attached to your little flailing fuzzball.

4. Map Variety Keeps It Fresh

From icy platforms to moving submarines, blimps, candy factories, and dangerous laboratories, the map design is clever. Some require skill, some require chaos — all of them feel different. The environmental hazards (like fans, crushers, and slippery floors) can turn the tide in hilarious ways.

🤕 What Doesn’t Work

1. The Controls Are... Mushy

Intentional or not, the controls are floaty and loose. Yes, it’s part of the charm, but it can also be frustrating when you try to do something precise — like pick up a weapon — and end up diving off the map like a sack of potatoes.

2. Online Can Be Laggy or Buggy

While much improved since launch, online play sometimes suffers from lag, disconnects, or weird hit detection. If you’re playing seriously (which you shouldn’t be), it can feel unfair when physics don’t behave the same across players.

3. Lack of Single-Player Content

There’s no story mode or real single-player experience. You can play solo against bots, but it’s not very engaging. This is a game meant entirely for social play — it’s not something you’ll grind alone.

4. Progression Feels a Bit Shallow

You unlock cosmetics and currency by playing, but the progression system isn’t very deep. If you're hoping for unlockable skills, customization, or deeper rewards — it's not that kind of game.

🐾 Final Score: 8/10

This game is a party game that copies off from Gang Beatz. But it's better in ways. If you really want to have actual fun with this game, please play this game with your friends. You'll laugh and feel angry at the same time. Depending on who is winning or losing. There's a lot to talk about this game I got when it was on sale. A mix of positive and negative. So let's get started.

First off, the game's mechanics feels a bit clunky. But it's meant to feel that way. It's highly recommended you play using a controller than using mouse and keys. The game offers a type of tutorial mode with the game's "Missions Mode." It's just 3 missions with a mix up of entertaining levels that make it feel that they could make a type of platforming beat'em up game. There are hidden rewards for completing the missions if you beat them fast enough, and find some achievements to further unlock more rewards. After finishing the tutorial, there's the main game that started the game, Last Stand. Followed by Smash, Team Games. Nemo Kart, and The Labs.

Last Stand is the game's main bread n' butter. 8 players in teams of 2 head to head to complete 3 rounds to win a set of the match battle royal. Each map having their own gimmick. An arena that slowly fills up with poison gas, to a room that generates a black hole to suck in the players to their death. So there's a wide variety of maps to play on. Each round also spawning weapons and power-ups for the players to use against the other players. Eliminating the other players in so many ways. That either help or harm their way into winning. Having a friend with you can ensure you and your friend will always play with each other in the team of 2. But having a team of 3 or 4 can ensure either playing Team Games or a rare chance of a Last Stand 4v4.

Team Games are a mix up of either sports type games, or gather and conquer type games with players of 4v4. From ice hockey to soccer and American Football, to collecting big candies in a candy factory for your team, or ensuring your team's train wins in a train race. There's also a chance you can play 4v4 last stand games with your party of 3 or 4.

Smash is a rogue-like game of Last Stand. But the maps change each round at random and you are given the choice of 1 of 3 random power-ups each round. Players can pick the same power-up that can further strengthen or even alter their abilities. Each round wins an amount of points instead of a round for your team. Each round giving more and more points. Whoever's team has the highest amount of points at the end of the 5 round match wins.

Nemo Kart is the game's version of...well, a Kart game rip-off of a franchise you may already know. I don't have to explain about how this game plays, If you know, you know. An 8 player racing kart game. Having it's whacky power-ups and you can earn "gears" that can let you buy more playable racing karts with different stats and performance. The higher the placement you win in the race, the more gears you can earn to buy the karts. However, this game mode is currently underutilized. There are only 4 maps to race on. 2 maps are the same map. But is now in reverse. The HUD does not have a map to tell you where you're on the race track and where the other players are at and their placement in the race. And the power-ups you pick up from the placements of the "?" crates depending on your placement in the race can be a little bit unfair at times. Another thing I have to point out here is there's not a lot of karts to unlock and buy. And there is a kart that is unfortunately that is OP, just using it can be an instant 1st place win for those who have it. Unless everyone is using it, then it's fair game. So hopefully they can balance this out, add more karts, and maps to this mode they've added.

All these game modes can all be played in the game's Quick Match and Custom Match. Playing Quick Match gains you experience points to level up to gain the game's in game currency and cosmetics. The more you play, the more characters and costumes for the characters you'll earn. There's also a weekly challenge list you can do to further gain more points and currency. However, they can all be played in Custom Game as well. But you'll not get a lot of experience points to do so. But can play this mode to try out any maps you haven't played yet and can play with bots to practice with. This is also the mode where you can invite all your friends to just have fun with all the games and maps it has to offer if you don't want to play with randoms in Quick Match. This also features a mode called, "The Labs."

The Labs is a variety of maps you can't play in the normal Last Stand games. Featuring a different mix of different maps that have different game play modes to win such as the subway to have your enemy team be run over by a train to win. Or The Winter Cabin that is now a hang out hub to have anyone to chat, or to play the card games that are featured in the cabin that can earn you its own currency to buy consumable items or even more character skins exclusively in that map. The 2 cards games being Pawz and Fishy Business. Pawz is the game's version of UNO. If you played UNO, I don't have to explain it. And both games have instructions to play these card games. So you can play them to have a calm moment from all the chaos. There is also a pirate game where you and a friend must fight against the opposing CPU enemies to defend your boat from being destroyed. And lastly, the latest game mode called "Crisis." Their version of Among Us.

Now I got some negatives I want to disclose here. The game you first pay money upfront to play, is also using a F2P system in the game. Remember the currencies I mentioned? Well, you can also buy real money to get them. Mainly Nemo Bucks it's premium currency. And you can simply pay to win the different costumes and characters you want to buy and not even bother. You can convert bucks into it's common currency "Cookies" to even get the costumes requiring it. Another thing I have to mention is the Surprise Eggs slot machine. Where characters are exclusive to this than being available in it's own store. Yes. You can earn the coins to get them from playing the game. Or you can use Nemo Bucks to take a spin at it. And to let you know, if you get the same character you already unlocked, then it will be converted it's common currency as Cookies. So buyer beware and don't turn it into gambling. The Item Store has different costumes and characters available each day and/or each week. Whether it would be the characters in a costume you wanted, or there is an IP Collab that you want to get and play as from another game or franchise. Just make sure you got enough to get them in advance. Another thing to add is that there are also event or holiday costumes you can buy. But they are limited time. And if you miss out, they might be gone for good. Giving this a bit of a FOMO approach.

There is one thing I must add onto as well. Once you hit max level in the game, currently level 150 as I write this, you are then given the chance to earn a random level up reward being an random amount of Cookies, Nemo Bucks, or Egg Coins. However, the game has a daily limit to how many you can earn. That being only 3 level ups a day. So if you didn't get the costume you wanted from the Surprise Egg machine or there was a costume or character you wanted to get this week and you didn't have enough currency to get it before the store resets, it's going to ask you to pay upfront for that premium currency to do so. However, I actually did manage to get plenty of the game's currency from just simply playing the game how it's intended and if you complete certain achievements, you'll have enough.

All and all, if they plan to add more to this game, Hopefully, this game will have some longevity onto doing so. They have a forums board.

General Thoughts
As someone who regularly hosts custom game fight nights for my friends, I can say that this game is incredibly fun. To me it is an example of what a party game should be: a fun, casual game that people can hop in at any skill level and have a blast with friends. You could play a single game and be done, or go all night until the sun comes up. I will say that the keyboard and mouse controls are a bit hard to get used to, especially with how the camera works. That said, the controller controls are solid, and clearly are the intended way to play. I doubt a fixed camera option would be possible, but something like that might make keyboard and mouse easier to play. 


Custom Games

As much as I love playing this game with friends, the custom games lack a surprising amount of customization compared to other party games. There is no way I have found to order the maps (aside from default ordering) or allow players to vote for the next map in custom games. There is no way to change which items are enabled or disabled, or change the frequency of item spawns (think super smash bros) or tweak the throwing costs of items. I would love to allow spectators to throw items as well, but there is no way to do this at the moment. 
There is also a minor issue with the afk kicking, where it can kick the host if they step away for a bit. A setting that turns this off or switches them to spectator (while retaining their score) would be nice to have. 

Friend Pass 

I absolutely love friend passes in games, as it helps me get other people into a game i can wholeheartedly recommend without having to pressure them into buying it. That way, they can try it out with me and get a feel for it themselves, before deciding if they want to spend the $20 on it. I think my only (highly specific) gripe with the pass is that if I leave a game or get kicked for afk, the person I'm sharing the pass with also gets kicked, even if there are other people on their list that we are playing with that have pass open (not being used). I understand that the actual code of making it switch to the next friend on their list would probably be more trouble than it's worth, but I figure i'd talk about it anyways. 


Game Modes
While there is a good variety of game modes available, I am a bit conflicted about them. I bought the game relatively early on, when there was just the last stand or team score game modes which I absolutely love. Since then, they've added a number of "lab" game modes that are pretty hit or miss for me. Overall, I prefer the game modes that are closer to their initial game style, with the other modes feeling pretty knockoff-ish. 

Winter Cabin: Good
The winter cabin isn't really a game mode, but rather a sandbox lobby that can be a free for all bar brawl or a casual hang out place to play a few mini games. The PAWS table game is just uno with a few different cards, and the other table game is just the Saboteur card game. Again, this is more of a space to chill and vibe in rather then throwing down, so it's a good map to hop in while you're waiting for people or taking a break. Again, having a way to turn the afk timer off would be nice here. I would also love to see a way to just keep the lobby open indefinitely, since there is still a game timer. 

Smash: Good but needs customization
The Smash game mode (as my friend described it) is the rouge-lite version of party animals, where you get permanent powers in between rounds. These buffs are pretty all over the place in terms of effects and balance, but overall are fun to play with. This is a mode that I would love to see have more customization available, with things like map voting, choosing which powers can be chosen, and how many choices you have per round (currently at 3 only). I would love to see more powers added, or maybe even a community event to brainstorm new powers. 

Final Destination: Good but needs customization
The closest thing they have to a true team death match style game mode, which is fun if you want to just throw down. This is another mode that I know would benefit from more customization and map variety,  and maybe more teams and players. Match timer, limit, and item spawns are an easy tweak that would help immensely. 

Black Sails: haven't played much
2 player max survival mode. From what I've seen it's fine, but the lack of larger lobby sizes is disappointing. In my mind this is a party game, and should have a 4 player MINIMUM for games. 

Nemo Kart: functional but beaten by competitors
at the launch of this game mode there was no way to change the controls, which were pretty strange compared to other games in the genre. this has been changed, but a bit of a rough start to say the least. The game mode functions, but is simply outclassed by games that focus on the racing genre, like mario kart. 

Space Crisis: haven't played, would probably just play the other games
From what I've heard, this is just the among us clone. There are plenty of other games in this genre that focus entirely on social deduction, so I would simply play those instead. (will update if i ever play this)


Monetization
I'd like to preface this by saying that I generally don't spend money on games aside from their initial purchase. That being said, I think paying in real money for cosmetics is fine, as they generally do not affect gameplay (save a few distracting or excessively dark cosmetics.) I have seen a lot of reviews regarding the recent claw machine system, being overtly difficult and costing premium currency, which I do agree should not be so difficult/chance based. Aside from that, I do not see any glaring issues with the monetization so far. 


Ending Thoughts
As someone who primarily plays this game in custom lobbies with friends and not in public matchmaking, I tentatively recommend this to anyone looking for a quick and casual game to play with a handful of friends. The lack of customization is technically functional but frustrating as someone who regularly hosts the lobbies. I feel like the new game modes are a poor way of attracting new players, as they basic in functionality and unrelated to the original game.
